title: The Fish's Eye
style_lock: Premium high-quality charming painted comic / Amar Chitra mythology; cream-saffron-gold cartouche; refined linework; Ep 10 field-master density; Arjuna and Krishna locked to Ep 09
camera: Heroic medium — named cast fills the frame, distant ranks only in the background
frame: Carved gold-and-lotus cartouche integrated into the painting (Ep 10 field-master / Ep 09 counsel) — not a thin rectangular sticker on a cream mat
prompt_prefix: Premium Amar Chitra / painted-comic illustration, native 3:2 canvas at least 1536×1024. Carved gold-and-lotus cartouche frame integrated into the artwork (not a thin sticker border, not a cream mat with four corner lotuses). Heroic medium shot: named figures fill the frame with engraved armor, refined linework, cream-saffron-gold hour. Not photoreal, not 16:9, not tiny distant heroes.

aim_geometry.eyes: Archer looks UP into the large ornamental ceiling mirror
aim_geometry.arrow: Arrow aims down at the fish eye in the ground pool
aim_geometry.stance: Archer stands on dry floor beside the pool, left side

apparatus.note: Studio visual of the BORI/Ganguli sky-yantra: ornamental mirror high under the roof; fish in the ground pool. Archer looks UP into the mirror and shoots the fish eye in the pool. No ceiling aquarium.

source_block.parva: Ādi Parva · Svayaṃvara · Draupadī’s lakṣya contest
source_block.divergence: BORI CE Ādi 176 and Ganguli CLXXXVII describe a stiff bow and a sky-yantra with a mark (lakṣya); they do not name a pool-fish. The series visual lock (AGENTS.md) reads that yantra as a ceiling mirror + ground-pool fish. BORI 179: kings fail to string; Arjuna as brahmin strings, five arrows, target falls pierced. Karna-insult / Draupadī refusing a sūta is later/vulgate colour, not BORI 179 — do not use it.
source_block.chosen: Gita Press Gorakhpur + BORI overlap: the contest itself — stiff bow, yantra-lakṣya, princes fail, Arjuna in brahmin guise hits the mark, Draupadī’s white varamāla. Visual apparatus follows the series lock (mirror + pool fish).
source_block.notes: Not TV. Krishna and Balarāma attend (Ganguli CLXXXVIII). Women of the court on upper mansions/balconies, not among princes on the floor.
